title: Common providers: Poland
coverage: Complete for the national fixed-line carrier, the four mobile network operators, the largest cable operators and the main wholesale fibre networks; business ISPs are partial.
missing: Local cable and fibre operators (several thousand undertakings are registered)
Smaller business ISPs and the city academic networks
AS numbers for the wholesale-only fibre networks Światłowód Inwestycje, Nexera and Polski Światłowód Otwarty (none found)

sources.name: UKE (Office of Electronic Communications): register of telecommunications undertakings
sources.terms: The page was requested on the read date; its reuse terms were not read (they are in the national language), so nothing is copied.
sources.result: The page answered on the read date. It is the authority to consult for operators this pack lacks.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Telecommunications in Poland
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Used to cross-check names only (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: 4 of 17 entries were found on the page, by their name or a distinctive other name.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Internet in Poland
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Used to cross-check names only (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: 4 of 17 entries were found on the page, by their name or a distinctive other name.

sources.name: Each provider's own public website
sources.terms: Only the address itself is recorded (a fact); no content is copied.
sources.result: 17 of 17 websites answered an automated check; an address that did not answer is left empty. No support or status page was checked.

sources.name: RIPEstat as-overview (RIPE NCC)
sources.terms: The RIPEstat terms forbid redistributing RIPEstat data: nothing is copied. Consulted to confirm, for each AS number, that the registered holder is the named provider.
sources.result: 19 AS numbers confirmed, each announced on the read date; a number whose holder was another company is listed only where the note says whose it is.

sources.name: RIPE Database (RIPE NCC): organisation and aut-num objects
sources.terms: The RIPE Database terms were not re-read for this pack; it is treated like RIPEstat data: nothing is copied. Consulted to find which AS numbers an organisation holds.
sources.result: Read to find candidate AS numbers; each was then confirmed as above.

sources.name: NRO delegated statistics (the regional registries' joint list of assigned AS numbers)
sources.terms: Published by the registries for public use; only which registry holds each AS number is taken (a fact).
sources.result: Every AS number in the pack was found in the list; its registry is recorded beside it.

sources.name: Wikipedia: UPC Polska
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0. Cited for a date and a name (facts); no text is copied.
sources.result: Read on the date above: the UPC name in Poland gave way to Play on 31 August 2023.

providers.name: Orange Polska
providers.notes: Fixed and mobile; the former Telekomunikacja Polska.

providers.name: Play
providers.notes: Mobile and cable. UPC Polska took this name on 31 August 2023; all three numbers are registered to P4.

providers.name: Plus
providers.notes: Mobile; the registered company is Polkomtel.

providers.name: Netia
providers.notes: Fixed lines for homes and business.

providers.name: Multimedia Polska
providers.notes: Cable. It holds its own AS number and is listed apart from Vectra, which its site names.

providers.name: Inea
providers.notes: Cable and fibre in the Poznań region.

providers.name: NASK
providers.notes: A state research institute that also sells lines (AS name NASK-COMMERCIAL).

providers.name: Fiberhost
providers.notes: Wholesale fibre access network; its site names Inea.
